blocks.text: Air pollution and bad air quality are responsible for huge economic costs and social and political issues.

items: Poor air quality reduces worker productivity through illness and absenteeism.
Air pollution damages crops, reducing agricultural yield and raising food prices.
Acid rain from air pollution degrades buildings, bridges and other infrastructure.
Vulnerable populations such as children, the elderly and low-income communities are disproportionately affected.
Chronic exposure to polluted air reduces the overall quality of life, affecting social well-being and community health.
Severe pollution can force people to migrate to areas with better air, causing social displacement and associated challenges.
Implementing effective air-quality regulations is challenging because of political and economic interests.
Air pollution is not confined by borders, so effective management requires international cooperation.
Regulation requires strict governance, which may slow industrial growth and economic development and lead to political conflict.
Addressing air pollution needs a multi-faceted approach balancing socio-economic and technological considerations.

blocks.prompt: Analyse the economic, social and political issues raised by a government plan to shut brick kilns during the smog season.
blocks.explanation: Economically the kilns' owners and labourers lose income and construction costs rise, against the savings in hospital bills, lost workdays and crop damage; socially the poorest workers bear the loss while the poorest neighbourhoods gain most in health; politically the owners lobby against the ban, enforcement needs strong governance, and because the smog drifts across provincial and national borders the plan works best with neighbouring regions acting together.

items: Economic: lost productivity, crop damage, infrastructure corrosion. Social: children, elderly and poor hit hardest; lower quality of life; migration. Political: interests resist regulation; pollution crosses borders (international cooperation); governance versus growth; multi-faceted balance needed.
